How I plan a video campaign from teaser to follow-up

A good launch needs more than a film and a release date. Here is how I plan the content around it.

Naqash BhattiDigital Campaign & Content Strategist

On this page

  1. Start with the people you want to reach
  2. Give each stage a purpose
  3. Make the team’s job easier
  4. Look at what happened, then adjust

When a client is releasing a brand film, the first question is not just when to post it. I want to know who needs to see it, what should happen before it goes live and what we will share afterwards.

Start with the people you want to reach

Before making the calendar, I ask a few basic questions. Who is this for? What do they already know? What would make them stop and watch? What should they do after seeing the film?

Give each stage a purpose

Teasers can build curiosity. Launch day is when the full story becomes clear. Follow-up edits give people something useful to share, remember or ask about after the main release.

Make the team’s job easier

I prepare the briefs, dates and asset list early. Designers, editors and advertising specialists should know what they are delivering, who approves it and when it needs to be ready.

Look at what happened, then adjust

Once content is live, I check the numbers in context. Views tell us something about distribution. Comments, enquiries and conversions tell us other things. The next step depends on what we actually learn.

A useful next step

Before your next launch, write down what you want people to think or do at each stage. It is a simple way to find gaps in the plan.
